Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Missouri State's injury report entering CUSA game against Delaware - AOL Skip to main content Advertisement Des Moin..., IA Des Moines, IA Local News Menu 24/7 Help For premium support please call: Sign in Mail 24/7 Help For premium support please call: Missouri State's injury report entering CUSA game against Delaware Liam Keating, Springfield News-Leader Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:11 PM UTC 0 Casey Woods provided an injury update to key starters Breezy Dubar, Ryan Mitchell and Mekhi Miller following the team's win over Kennesaw State. SPRINGFIELD — There’s little time to dwell and celebrate Missouri State’s win over Kennesaw State on Wednesday, Oct. 14. The Bears (2-4, 1-1 in CUSA) are moving on to its next Conference USA clash against Delaware (2-4, 0-2) on Tuesday, Oct. 20. Against the Owls, Missouri State was without three key players on the offensive side of the ball. Missouri State was down three starters in running back Breezy Dubar, offensive lineman Ryan Mitchell and wide receiver Mekhi Miller. “Two guys are concussion guys that I expect we get back this week being Breezy and Ryan,” Woods said. Missouri State: Casey Woods pushes for more Group of Six representation in expanded CFP Missouri State: Jmariyae Robinson one step closer to the triple crown As for Miller, the fifth-year player suffered an injury during pregame warmups against Kennesaw State. Woods does not know the extent of the injury as of Thursday, Oct. 15. “Mekhi had a weird thing come up pregame,” Woods said. “We are still doing some more. I don’t have enough information to get you exactly what’s going on with that right now.” Dubar has rushed for 218 yards, which ranks second-best on the team. He’s also tied with Ramone Green Jr. with two touchdowns for the most on the roster. Mitchell featured on the offensive line in every game before missing the last game. Miller is Missouri State’s third-best wide receiver option. He has 13 catches for 146 yards. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. The No. 5 Hoosiers play host to the fourth-ranked Buckeyes with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to the Big Ten Championshiop Game in Indianapolis The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warm-up for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss). Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith , who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category. This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Ohio State vs. Indiana: Need to know Annual top-five matchup: For the first 97 meetings between these teams, there were zero top-five matchups. When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands. Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year. Sacking Sayin: One way to make sure Smith never gets the football is to hit Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin while he still has the ball. That's exactly what the Hoosiers did in the Big Ten title game, sacking Sayin five times. Indiana has the personnel to get after Sayin again this time around. Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical. Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction, picks This should be another tremendous game between a pair of national title contenders, and it may very well be a preview of the Big Ten Championship matchup. Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time. Ohio State hits enough big plays with Smith to create some breathing room late. As for the Hoosiers, they have scored at least 20 in every outing in 2026. Then again, Indiana scored six points through three quarters last Saturday at Nebraska. And, on the flip side, Ohio State hasn’t seen a defense half as sturdy as Indiana’s, aside from Texas, which held the Buckeyes to only three points in the second half. If Indiana’s defense strings together four full quarters, it can bottle up this Ohio State offense – or at least keep it at bay (Smith won’t be entirely shut down by any defense this year). And the expectation is that the Hoosiers offense, which has sputtered at times this year, struggles with this Buckeyes defense. It’d be a surprise to see either team score three touchdowns. picks.headline: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7?
picks.blurb: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7? Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB This game needs no introduction. Some may argue this is the game Ohio State has been preparing fo r all season long . Now it has a chance to go to Indiana and rewrite a wrong from last December, when it lost the Big Ten Championship game to the Hoosiers, which ultimately led to them completing their undefeated season. Ohio State isn’t undefeated like Indiana is. However, the Buckeyes are rolling through the start of the Big Ten schedule without any real hiccups. Ohio State (5-1, 3-0 Big Ten) has had this game against the Hoosiers (6-0, 3-0 Big Ten) earmarked on the schedule since it was released. So much so that both teams have remained the class of the Big Ten all year long, with a possible elimination scenario in play come December, ahead of the Big Ten title game in Indianapolis. Someone’s supremacy must be disrupted . Will the Buckeyes struggle again, or will the Hoosiers exploit their weaknesses? Check out our staff picks as the game gets underway. Ohio State vs. Indiana Week 7 Outlook Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day watches during the NCAA football game against the Maryland Terrapins at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: noon ET/9 a.m. PT TV Channel: FOX (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds: Ohio State -3; over/under is 50.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Memorial Stadium – Bloomington, Ind. Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 87-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. Indiana: A 13-10 loss in the Big Ten title game in a top-two showdown. Ohio State leads the series dating back to 1989, 31-1-1. Pregame festivities: Big Noon Kickoff will be there. Ohio State so far this season: 5-1 (3-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando: 6-0 Dylan Buganski : 5-1 Rafael Zamorano : 4-1 (no pick in Week 6 nor Week 7) Chip Minnich : 4-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 28, Indiana 24 There is no such thing as a one-game season, but the Buckeyes may beg to differ. Indiana handed Ohio State one of its two back-to-back losses to end last season and now, on a fall Saturday in Bloomington, the entire year could come down to whether Ohio State can finally sneak up and regain head-to-head dominance and steal a road win. If wideout Jeremiah Smith gets space and gets comfortable thanks to Julian Sayin, and forces the defense to tire Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover, the game could easily deliver a fantastic finish in the closing minutes. We’ll see if the Buckeyes can make it interesting, or better yet, secure a road win that could change the season for good. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 31, Indiana 28 The highly anticipated, top-five Big Ten showdown between the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday hinges on how Ryan Day's squad handles sudden depth issues against an elite Indiana defense. Ohio State faces an uphill battle following a troubling availability report ruling out two of the team's most relied-upon members on offense ~ Austin Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson. With Austin Siereveld missing his second straight game, the loss of the Preseason All-Big Ten selection strips the Buckeyes of their offensive line leader. This forces Gabe VanSickle and right tackle Phillip Daniels into hyper-extended roles against a vicious Hoosier pass rush; Daniels has not played since the loss at Texas on September 12th. Ja'Kobi Jackson, the team's powerhouse short-yardage back and touchdown leader (6 TDs), is sidelined with a surprise ankle injury. While Bo Jackson will shoulder the primary workload, Ja'Kobi Jackson's absence eliminates the physical lightning-and-thunder dynamic Ohio State uses to control the tempo. Could Isaiah West, who missed a key block that led to a pick-six interception in last week's Maryland game, get a chance at redemption? West offers a physical style of play comparable to Ja'Kobi Jackson. The fans who have been clamoring for Legend Bey may see Bey as a larger part of the offensive game plan. Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith will need to be creative in the run game and involve other receiving talents beyond Jeremiah Smith. With a depleted ground game and a reshuffled protection unit, the entire game plan in my estimation rests on the shoulders of junior quarterback Julian Sayin. Sayin has been using his legs to gain positive yardage in recent games and may need to run more frequently than desired by Sayin or the Ohio State coaching staff. The Ohio State defense is going to be tested, as Indiana boasts talented wide receivers in Nick Marsh and Charlie Becker, plus a strong running game led by Turbo Richard. Quarterback Josh Hoover has not yet thrown an interception this season, so perhaps Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia will be able to scheme some situations that result in a turnover. Expect a classic, physical Big Ten chess match. While Indiana enters the match healthier and with a strong defensive front, Sayin's elite talent and postseason poise will provide just enough explosive plays in a late two-minute drill to secure a tight, field-goal victory for the Buckeyes in Bloomington. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, Indiana 17 There may not be a matchup this team as well as fans circled coming into this season then the rematch of last year’s Big Ten Championship game in what may be Indiana’s biggest home game in program history. There are old and new faces on both sides, and the clash between head coaches Ryan Day and Curt Cignetti may become one of the conference’s greatest rivalries going forward. Ohio State comes into this matchup battle-tested, seeing ranked teams Iowa and Texas on the road and finishing 1-1 in those matchups. This will be Indiana’s first ranked matchup of the season, but they had a comeback victory at Nebraska last week, in which the Cornhuskers should probably have been a ranked team. This matchup will come down to how dominant Indiana can be at the line of scrimmage, as that may be the only position where Indiana may have more talent than the Buckeyes, other than maybe running back. Indiana should be able to run the ball decently and stop the run on the other side. away.headline: Ohio State football releases first injury report vs. Indiana: Who’s in, who’s out for the Buckeyes
away.blurb: Offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who missed last week’s win against Maryland, was deemed out on Wednesday’s injury report — the first of four reports this week. Running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, who has appeared in every game for the Buckeyes this season, was also listed as out. He has started the last two games for Ohio State, though running back Bo Jackson had more carries in both contests. Receiver Brock Boyd, running back Isaiah West, defensive end Khary Wilder and offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were listed as questionable. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, defensive back Jay Timmons, offensive tackle Phillip Daniels and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the report, suggesting they’ll be available after missing last week’s win vs. Maryland. While Timmons could return this week, safety Leroy Roker — who has also been sidelined since Sept. 26 — was listed as out. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State plays at Indiana on Saturday in one of the biggest games of the college football regular season. However, the Buckeyes won’t be at full strength for the matchup. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

away.headline: Ohio State announces injury update on quarterback Julian Sayin
away.blurb: Starting quarterback Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with a forearm injury after taking a massive hit from the pocket. He later returned to the sideline with his arm in a sling. After the game, Ohio State head coach Ryan Day announced that Sayin would be out for “several weeks.” Ohio State held on to win after Indiana wide receiver Nick Marsh stepped out of bounds on what could’ve been a game-winning touchdown pass late in the fourth quarter. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover had Marsh open, but he was barely out of bounds, giving Ohio State the win. Ohio State notched a massive win over Indiana on Saturday, but it came at a cost. MORE: College football games on today, Week 7 AP Top 25 TV schedule for Saturday Sayin finished the game with 235 yards through the air, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey replaced him and didn’t complete a pass. What happened after Sayin got hurt? The loss snapped Indiana’s 22-game winning streak since the program went undefeated last year and was 6-0 at the start of this season. Who replaces Sayin going forward? The favorite to start is Fahey, a three-star recruit in the 2026 recruiting class, per 247Sports Composite rankings . He was the No. 586 overall recruit in the country before enrolling at Ohio State. Ohio State is 6-1 overall and will play USC in its next game on Halloween after a bye week next weekend. We’ll see if Sayin can make his way back to the lineup before the end of the season.

away.headline: Ohio State football got a freshman back from injury at Indiana — and his star power was evident
away.blurb: That’s when Timmons stepped in. The Pennsylvania native punched the ball out before Chandler hit the turf. Ohio State recovered the fumble, ending an Indiana drive during the middle eight minutes of the game. That sequence from Timmons proved to be pivotal, with Ohio State’s offense mustering only 19 points on a day when quarterback Julian Sayin struggled before suffering a right-arm injury that’ll keep him out “several weeks,” per coach Ryan Day . The unit’s momentum carried into the win at Indiana, with Timmons playing a key role in his return. However, he couldn’t finish the contest. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Jay Timmons was an under-the-radar champion of the Ohio State offseason, emerging as a true freshman capable of starting for defensive coordinator Matt Patricia. He impressed in spring practice drills, worked his way up the depth chart in preseason camp and solidified himself as the Buckeyes’ top nickelback by Week 1. His performance in Saturday’s 19-15 win at Indiana was a reminder of how Timmons’ rise was possible. The former five-star prospect is a playmaker — one that has shown up for Ohio State in the biggest moments, even as Timmons has battled injury. The Hoosiers learned that, when healthy, he’s among the Buckeyes’ most dangerous defensive players. Indiana opened the second half with its offense on the field, trailing 10-7 after losing momentum late in the first half. Quarterback Josh Hoover seemed to have his team trending back in the right direction, though, with a 19-yard completion to Davion Chandler on the second play from scrimmage in the half. The Buckeyes only managed to score three points on the ensuing drive, giving the Hoosiers a chance to move past the fumble. They started strong, with Hoover finding star receiver Charlie Becker for a 36-yard completion. Timmons, again, prevented Indiana from finding further success. On the first-down play following Becker’s catch, Indiana threw a screen pass to Tyler Morris. He seemed to have an open field ahead of him, only needing to get past a freshman defensive back. Timmons won the battle, taking down Morris for no gain. He added a pass breakup on second down and a tackle short of the line to gain on third. While impressive, Timmons’ performance wasn’t surprising. He played 62 defensive snaps in Ohio State’s Week 2 loss at Texas — the first ranked matchup of the freshman’s career. He forced a fumble on his first play from scrimmage and delivered a big hit on quarterback Arch Manning later in the contest. Timmons remained a regular part of Ohio State’s defense in the weeks that followed, but an injury late in a Sept. 26 win against Illinois sidetracked his season. Timmons missed games against Iowa and Maryland — contests that saw Ohio State’s defense take a step forward after a shaky first quarter of the regular season. away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect With the Buckeyes' star quarterback out "several weeks," and challenging Big Ten opponents on deck, the trajectory of Ohio State's season is very much up in the air Josh Hoover finds Nick Marsh - BUT HE'S OUT OF BOUNDS pic.twitter.com/WCcs1mUefF But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. Manning's inconsistency has kept the Longhorns' offense largely out of rhythm this season, a critique he'll try to correct against the SEC's worst defense. After a loss to rival Oklahoma sent the Longhorns falling six spots in the AP Poll, Texas is hoping to use the tailspinning Gators as their punching bag to stay in the College Football Playoff picture. Florida has lost back-to-back SEC games in blowout fashion , tumbling out of the national rankings without a clear solution to stop the hemorrhaging. Sumrall said progress is sometimes "dysfunctional" and agreed with some of the booing he experienced on the sideline of last week's loss to South Carolina . The Gators struggled to block Gamecocks edge Dylan Stewart and now must endure the athleticism of Colin Simmons , who leads college football with 9.5 sacks. Simmons collected five sacks during a win at Tennessee last month and is the runaway favorite to win the SEC's Defensive Player of the Year honor. Where to watch Texas vs. Florida live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium -- Austin, Texas TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Texas vs. Florida: Need to know Turnovers and touchdowns: Manning's production against Power Four competition has been pedestrian -- four touchdown passes and four interceptions. Two came during the fourth quarter of last week's loss to Oklahoma, including a pick-six that swung the game's momentum to the Sooners. Manning's been sacked 12 times through five games -- 10 coming against Ohio State , Tennessee and Oklahoma. If there's a get-right opportunity for Florida's defense, perhaps this is it. Frightening defensive numbers: Florida ranks last in the SEC in total defense, explosive plays allowed, pass defense and 15th in scoring defense this season. Sumrall said this week he was taking a closer look at multiple areas of his team to try and fix what has nuked this 4-0 start for the Gators. It starts with getting stops on defense against the Longhorns. Longhorns' second 'revenge' game: A failure-to-show loss against the Gators in Gainesville ultimately kept Texas out of the CFP last year. Now, Sarkisian's squad has a chance to move to 2-0 this season in revenge opportunities after beating Ohio State in Week 2. Texas remains in this week's updated CFP projection with a first-round home game and has a clear-cut path to the 12-team bracket, but Saturday's a must-win. Texas vs. Florida prediction, picks Texas has problems on offense, but Florida's even worse on defense. Consecutive SEC blowouts have erased the goodwill from a 4-0 start and No. 8 ranking, and a secondary LaNorris Sellers picked apart last week now gets Manning. Consistency hasn't been Manning's calling card, but this matchup should restore some confidence in the Longhorns' passing game. Florida isn't giving anyone reason to trust its defense, especially against an opponent with something to prove. Last season's loss to the Gators should have Texas' attention. The Longhorns return the favor this weekend. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Covers custom image. Florida and Texas square off in a high-stakes SEC showdown Saturday, with both programs looking to bounce back from disappointing losses. The Gators have dropped two straight, including a lopsided defeat to South Carolina, while the Longhorns are looking to regroup after falling to rival Oklahoma and surrendering their No. 1 ranking. Our Florida vs. Texas prediction backs the Longhorns to cover the 10.5-point spread, but our college football expert sees even better value in the game total. Read on for our analysis and more college football picks for Saturday's slate. Who will win Florida vs Texas: Texas -10.5 Have the Florida Gators been "figured out"? I'm not sure. Has Florida had extreme regression over the last few games and probably gotten to a record it should be, even if it required some extremely unbalanced games to do so? Probably so. I'm taking the Texas Longhorns to cover this -10.5 number; it's a small edge, and I wouldn't play it past here. Florida's offense is (still) legit, ranking 8th in EPA per pass, but the defense has been a sieve. The Gators rank 123rd in success rate allowed (49.7%) and dead last at 136th in 3rd/4th down success allowed, so Texas doesn't need to be explosive to sustain drives. They need to be solid, which is pretty much the definition of an Arch Manning-led offense. On the other side, the Longhorns' defense ranks 2nd nationally in adjusted EPA per play, 9th against the run and 11th against the pass, while allowing just 29.9% of available yards (5th) . Florida won't trade scores all afternoon. I'll lay it. TOP PICK Florida vs Texas Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 I'm playing the Under 51.5 and would take it down to 50.5 (50%). It's my top pick. Florida's offense has been efficient, but it hasn't faced a defense that controls early downs as Texas does. The Longhorns rank 5th nationally in early-down EPA per play allowed, which has opponents facing an average 3rd down distance of 8.12 yards , 15th in the country. Florida already ranks 105th in average 3rd down distance at 7.62 yards , so expect a lot of long-yardage situations and stalled drives. Texas also ranks 6th in defensive EPA per drive, so even when the Gators move the ball, points haven't come easily against this unit. The Texas offense isn't built to push this total either. It ranks 55th in success rate and 67th in EPA per pass, and gains just 46.5% of available yards (70th). Expect the Longhorns to win with long, methodical drives that drain the clock rather than quick-strike scores. Florida vs Texas combo This combo is built around one game script: Florida hangs around early, then Texas takes over. Coming off two straight blowouts, the Gators should come out with urgency, and an offense that ranks 8th in EPA per pass can keep them close for a half. Texas's offense isn't built to jump out to fast leads either. The second half is where the Longhorns' advantages show up. Florida's defense ranks dead last in 3rd-and-4th down success allowed, and long Texas drives should wear the Gators down, pull away on the scoreboard, and eat clock to keep this under the total. Florida 1st Half +6.5 Florida vs Texas prop: Florida Under 2.5 touchdowns Florida has been able to move the ball this season, but finishing drives against this Texas defense is a different story. The Longhorns hold opponents to a 38.8% passing success rate (25th) and rank 6th in defensive EPA per drive, so even productive Gators possessions are likely to stall short of the end zone. With Texas expected to control the ball on long drives, Florida's opportunities will be limited, and field goals are the more likely outcome when it does get into scoring range. Coming off a loss, Texas is eager to get back in the conference title picture with a good showing against the reeling Gators. Here's what you need to know heading into the matchup as The Big Lead locks in our final prediction for this Week 7 college football clash. Texas offensive inconsistency and defensive strength Arch Manning has shown flashes but has been uneven against better competition, with turnovers becoming a recurring issue. Pass protection has been mixed despite solid grades in some metrics, and the run game has lacked consistent explosiveness. Where Texas separates itself is on defense. The unit ranks among the better groups nationally in yards allowed and has been especially effective limiting yards after contact. Rushing off the edges and overall tackling efficiency have been strengths. That could create some real problems for a Florida offense that has looked worn down. Defensive collapse, run game issues at Florida NCAA Football: Mississippi at Florida Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Even during the Gators' win streak, critics sounded the alarm about this defense. The two-game skid has confirmed those worries. Missed tackles and coverage breakdowns have piled up? The total damage? Florida is the SEC's worst defense in total output, explosive plays allowed, and against the pass. It's the second-worst in scoring. On offense, the Florida run game that once looked dominant has been largely shut down by better fronts. Jadan Baugh's production has dropped sharply. After rushing for over 130 yards in four wins, his totals fell to 13 and then 59 yards in two losses. Questions also linger about quarterback availability with Aaron Philo listed as questionable. A potential shift to Tramell Jones Jr. would add even more uncertainty against a Texas defense that flies to the ball. Key matchup dynamics to watch Texas holds clear edges in defensive structure and home-field stability. Florida's ability to create explosive plays through play-action and yards after catch remains a theoretical strength, but recent film shows those opportunities drying up against disciplined units. Scheme-wise, Texas' ability to limit perimeter runs and finish tackles aligns poorly with what Florida has relied on. Manning should face less pressure than he did against Oklahoma, giving him cleaner looks against a secondary that has been vulnerable. Florida vs. Texas prediction: Who wins and why? Texas is the more complete team right now, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Even with offensive questions, the Longhorns' ability to control the line of scrimmage and force Florida into obvious passing situations should decide the game. Florida has the talent to keep stretches competitive, but the recent defensive regression and limited run game make a full road upset unlikely. The Big Lead Prediction: Texas 31, Florida 17

picks.blurb: Florida vs. Texas Final Score Predictions: Experts weigh in on a desperate Gators team heading to Austin - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Hurts reportedly out for season NFL news, updates Rays take 3-2 ALCS lead NFL Winners and Losers WNBA Finals Game 2 preview Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun-Imagn Images, Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 15, 2026 at 6:48 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After suffering back-to-back embarrassing losses, can the Florida Gators get back in the win column against a reeling Texas Longhorns team? The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. A win here would do wonders to get them back in our good graces. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. But a victory would right the ship for the Longhorns, especially if beleaguered quarterback Arch Manning and an error-prone special teams can trim the mistakes and play a clean game. Under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and breakout running back Jadan Baugh , Florida became one of the early-season darlings of college football after knocking off Ole Miss and climbing into the top 10 of the AP rankings. But the Gators have fallen out of the poll following two straight losses, and a porous Florida defense has given up a combined 83 points over the past two weeks to Missouri and South Carolina. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Florida Gators. He's thrown for 1,341 yards on 70.5% passing with nine touchdowns and three interceptions and has added 104 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Florida could test that pair as well as the rest of the secondary if healthy, but that's a big question mark entering Saturday's game. away.headline: Florida injury report: Philo, Brown, Stockton game-time decisions
away.blurb: Running back Duke Clark remains out and will not be available to play. Quarterback Aaron Philo and wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton are all listed as game-time decisions ahead of the noon ET kickoff. Philo's status has been one of the biggest questions of the week. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reported Wednesday that he had been limited in practice as he recovered from a shoulder injury. Presumably, it occurred on a fourth-quarter scramble against South Carolina last Saturday, after which he was pulled for a play and eventually the game. picks.headline: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why?
picks.blurb: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB After LSU traveled to Lexington last weekend, Lane Kiffin and the Tigers are coming off of a disappointing loss, heading into the Week 7 matchup against Mississippi State . LSU heads into the matchup with a recent loss, while the Bulldogs are also traveling to Baton Rouge after a loss to the Crimson Tide in Week 5. Before the No. 22 LSU Tigers host the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday, the LSU On SI team predicts which team will win and why. Oct 3, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers safety Tamarcus Cooley (0) intercepts a pass from McNeese Cowboys quarterback Jake Strong (not pictured) during the first half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud The time for sloppiness is over, and everyone in LSU’s football program knows it. Ole Miss was a game you could’ve won. Kentucky was a game you should never have lost. That will be LSU’s wake-up call. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. LSU 44, Mississippi State 21 Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Adrian Ramirez Adrian Ramirez LSU will bounce back from its overtime loss to Kentucky with a strong performance at home in Tiger Stadium. If both Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell miss or are limited by their injuries, I expect LSU’s defense to be too much for Mississippi State to handle. I think the Tigers come out with a point to prove and get to work proving it. LSU 31, Mississippi State 14 Hannah Garcia While there’s the possibility of Taylor and Bothwell being out for the game, the LSU defense is still missing key pieces in Spears and Whit Weeks. The receivers have struggled to find consistency all season with catching the ball and Sam Leavitt’s interception numbers are also something that I think could cause LSU to lose. Mississippi State 24, LSU 17 LSU is desperate to bounce back after a tough loss against Kentucky. The keys to this game are Kamario Taylor’s health and Mississippi State’s secondary. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs allow the second-most passing yards per game in the SEC, so I expect Lane Kiffin to open up the playbook and attack that weakness. I think the Tigers handle business at home. LSU 35, Mississippi State 21 Published Oct 16, 2026 BROOKE BENEDICT Brooke Benedict is a sophomore at LSU, majoring in journalism. She is originally from Boulder, Colorado, and enjoys skiing, hiking, and Pilates. She's always enjoyed watching sports and the way sports bring people together. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:20 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It looked like LSU was about to dominate the college football world when it beat Clemson 51-10 to start the season. But Lane Kiffin's bunch lost to Ole Miss, came back with a few wins, and then last week got outfoxed by Kentucky in a 35-34 overtime loss. And now there's a problem. LSU is talented enough to beat anyone, but it's one more loss away from realistically being out of the College Football Playoff. That won't be easy with a brutal schedule over the second half of the season. Mississippi State has had two weeks to get over the 56-23 loss to Alabama. It isn't an easy slate, but at 4-1, it'll still be in the mix for big things if it can get out of Baton Rouge with a win. Mississippi State vs LSU: Quick Hits LSU starts a run of three home games in the next four weeks, going to Auburn next before hosting Alabama and Texas. Mississippi State starts its own run of four home games in five weeks after this, hosting Oklahoma before going to Texas. LSU has won three straight in the series ever since the 44-34 loss to open up the 2020 season. That came right after the Tigers' national title season. How To Watch Mississippi State vs LSU Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Mississippi State Will Win The defense will have to step up its game. The Bulldogs have been winning on their amazing offense, but the defense has held its own in key spots. It might be tough to hang with the Tigers blow for blow, so taking the ball away is a must. Mississippi State came up with two takeaways in two of the last three games, and turnovers have been a big issue for LSU, with ten in six games. Why does the defense have to come up big? Why LSU Will Win Mississippi State might be without star quarterback Kamario Taylor. He's trying to get past a leg injury suffered in the Alabama loss, and now he and top running back Fluff Bothwell are questionable at best. There's also the home-field advantage side of this. Ole Miss and Kentucky are good, but LSU should've been better in both road games. At home, the Tigers have been untouchable, winning by a combined score of 194-44 in the four games. Mississippi State vs LSU Prediction, Betting Lines It'll be a different LSU team than the one that walked off the field against Kentucky. It'll be more confident, explosive, and it won't let up – this won't be a back-and-forth fight like it was against the Wildcats. Of course, this changes if Taylor is at 100% for the Bulldogs, but even if he's ready to roll, LSU will be razor-sharp with a much better defensive performance than last week. For those unfamiliar, Havoc is the collection of stats that can derail offensive momentum on the defensive side of the ball, including tackles for loss, pass breakups, forced fumbles, interceptions and sacks. Havoc allowed, meanwhile, is a stat used to quantify an offense's ability to avoid chaos that creates a negative play. Offenses that are elite in Havoc allowed have a low number of fumbles, interceptions and tackles for loss allowed. Led by edge Princewill Umanmielen, the Tigers also boast a top-10 pass rush and continue to haunt opposing quarterbacks in passing downs. The aggressiveness should pay off for defensive coordinator Blake Baker in Week 7 against a Mississippi State team coming off a bye week. college football-picks-havoc rankings-prediction-mississippi state vs lsu-week 7 The Bulldogs will come off a bye week with a trip to Baton Rouge. Mississippi State was humbled on offense against Alabama in Week 5, surrendering 21 pressures and six sacks. The health of Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell could be news in the late-week SEC Availability Report after both suffered lower-body injuries. Can Lane Kiffin and the Tigers bounce back after an embarrassing loss? The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. How Each Team Wins For LSU, everything starts with protecting the football. Leavitt must avoid costly interceptions and take advantage of Mississippi State's vulnerable secondary. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Auburn Tigers in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry on Saturday afternoon. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. No, it's not nearly as fierce as the Iron Bowl when Alabama takes on Auburn, but when you've played 130 times, you tend to have a few interesting moments that build into something generational. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. Auburn vs Georgia: Quick Hits Auburn gets LSU and the Lane Kiffin show next, and then goes to Ole Miss. Georgia gets a week off before playing the Cocktail Party showdown against Florida in Atlanta, and then it goes to Ole Miss. Georgia has won seven times in the series since losing in 2017 (it was No. 1 in the nation then, too), but it won the SEC Championship a few weeks later. The Bulldogs have won 11 of the last 12 meetings. It might have been hit hard by Florida, but it does a lot of bending without breaking, thanks to plenty of sacks, lots of plays behind the line, and a third down defense that's holding up well. Offensively, the high-tempo Tiger attack should be able to keep the Bulldogs on their heels. Alabama ran well last week, but it only handed the ball off 29 times. Auburn won't make that mistake, pushing for at least 35 carries, and close to 40, as it tries to hit the Georgia defense with tempo. Why Georgia Will Win Georgia's defensive front will live in the Auburn backfield. It's a problem with Auburn's style that it allows defenses to tee off on the quarterback and come up with too many tackles for loss. The Tigers don't worry about the time of possession battle, and they're good at overcoming negative plays with something positive, but Georgia has the defense to swarm all over the quick-hitting short plays. Auburn doesn't do anything deep, and Georgia should limit any yards after the catch or runs that get to the second level. Auburn vs Georgia Prediction, Betting Lines It's been an interesting start to the Golesh era. The offense is supposed to dominate and take over, but it doesn't do it enough. The defense that was so great last year has stayed strong, but it's about to get pounded on. Auburn's two losses came when it allowed over three yards per carry. Georgia is averaging over six yards per pop. away.headline: Georgia football injury report: Another starter ruled out for Auburn
away.blurb: Starting Georgia safety KJ Bolden is officially out for Saturday’s clash with Auburn in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry. In Friday’s SEC Availability Report , the Bulldogs downgraded Bolden from doubtful to out. Georgia ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion , sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear , junior running back Chauncey Bowens , junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green on Wednesday with the first report of the week. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Bolden came off the field slowly late in Georgia’s win over Alabama after tallying 7 tackles (3 solo), a half tackle for loss and a half sack. After the game, he was wearing a heavy wrap around his left calf muscle. Bolden’s streak of 34 straight games played to start his Georgia career is in jeopardy. He has started 19 of the last 20, missing one first half due to a targeting penalty in the previous game. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since. The Bulldogs and Tigers tee it up at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. Georgia will enjoy its only bye of the season in Week 8.

The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents. Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama. While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell leads the league in passing yards with 1,599 and brings game-changing mobility. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary. The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020. Where to watch Alabama vs. Tennessee live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Neyland Stadium -- Knoxville, Tennessee TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. Tennessee: Need to know Neyland blues: The last time Tennessee beat a ranked team at Neyland Stadium was in 2024, when it edged No. 7 Alabama 24-17. The Vols finished 0-3 at home against ranked opponents last season and fell 20-17 to Texas in Week 4, extending their home losing streak against ranked opponents to four games. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time. Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon . Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver. Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. A loss would drop that mark to 52.9% and crush Alabama's margin for error. Because the Crimson Tide's strength of schedule lags behind others in the SEC, its case for inclusion as a three-loss team would be shaky. Tennessee's playoff odds would shoot to 51.6% with a win and drop to 16.8% with a loss. Alabama vs. Tennessee prediction, picks Tennessee's defense and run game have carried it to a 5-1 start. Replicating that formula against Alabama won't be possible unless the Crimson Tide shoot themselves in the foot with turnovers and special team miscues. Because the Crimson Tide won't respect the Volunteers' passing game, they'll be able to load the box and frustrate Tennessee's ground game, much like Texas did in Week 4. Offensively, Alabama has too much firepower to be fully restrained for four quarters. Look for Bama to pull away in the fourth quarter. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs Tennessee: Alabama -7.5 If last week was any indicator, Tennessee has far more problems than Alabama , despite the Volunteers' win and the Crimson Tide's loss. In George MacIntyre's first start for Josh Heupel, he finished with just a 10.3 QBR in a seven-point win against Arkansas. He'll be starting again against Bama, which is why I like the Tide to cover -9.5 or better . Arkansas lost to its previous three Power Four opponents by an average of 29.3 points, including a 28-point defeat to Georgia — the same team Alabama lost to by just three on the road last week. Tennessee's offense won't be able to keep up with Alabama. Keelon Russell ranks third nationally in QBR (90.0) , and the Tide are top 20 in offensive success rate (50.1%). The Alabama vs. Tennessee rivalry history is full of winning streaks, and this could be the start of another. Alabama vs Tennessee Over/Under pick: Over 50.5 For this Over to hit (I'd take it at 51.5 or better ), Alabama will need to do the bulk of the scoring, and the Tide will push for 31+ points given Russell's recent play. His dual-threat ability has helped open up the run game, too, with Alabama ranking fourth nationally in rush success rate (53.3%) . That will force Jim Knowles' defense to stay honest instead of solely focusing on protecting the back end. Meanwhile, Tennessee should be able to put up 20+ points to help push the total Over. The Volunteers have one of the best run games in the country (No. 2 in EPA per rush), led by DeSean Bishop . Bishop ranks top 10 nationally in rushing yards after contact (465). Alabama vs Tennessee prop: Alabama team total Over 29.5 Given how loaded Alabama's offense is, I like the Over at 30.5 or better , especially with how the Tide matchup against Tennessee's defense. Even with Ryan Coleman-Williams out, Alabama remains loaded at the skill positions, with eight other players topping 180 yards from scrimmage this season. That includes Lotzeir Brooks , who leads the Tide in yards per route run (2.76). Russell, Brooks, and Co. should take advantage of a Volunteers defense that's 70th nationally in pass success rate (43.9%). Alabama rarely squanders opportunities either, ranking third in the country in points per opportunity (5.27) . Alabama vs Tennessee combo One word describes Tennessee's passing game: rocky. The Volunteers are 128th nationally in pass success rate (33.8) , and MacIntyre has a QBR of 24.7 this season. That won't cut it against an Alabama defense tied for the 14th-most sacks in the country (17). I'm expecting a fast start from Russell after last week's tough loss to Georgia, and once Bama takes the lead, Tennessee isn't equipped to come back with MacIntyre behind center. The Tide, who are ninth nationally on defense in rush success rate (35.4%), should be able to focus on slowing Bishop enough to win by 10+ points. Best Alabama vs Tennessee props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Over 240.5 Pass Yards (53.27%) Alabama star sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell should be amped up to bounce back after an underwhelming 16-for-30, 185-yard performance with just one touchdown in the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. That said, it came against arguably the best defense in the country. It was Russell's worst performance since throwing for just 188 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Week 2 against Kentucky. Over six games this season, Russell still averages more than this prop at 266.5 passing yards per game. He draws a Tennessee defense that has shut down quarterbacks all season, allowing just 185 passing yards per game. However, what elite quarterback have the Volunteers actually shut down? "Well, they held Arch Manning to just 201 yards." Oh, like that holds up in the year of our Lord 2026. Russell is far better than Manning and has faced far tougher competition this season than what this Volunteers pass defense has seen. Coming off a matchup against one of the country's best defenses, the sophomore should clear 240 passing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 250.5 passing yards. Prop pick #2: DeSean Bishop Over 89.5 Rush Yards (50.74%) With Tennessee's run-heavy offense averaging nearly 43 rushing attempts per game this season, I don't expect that approach to change on Saturday against a very talented Alabama run defense. Over their last three games against Texas, Auburn, and Arkansas, the Volunteers still average 38.33 attempts per game . Tennessee should lean on its leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , to move the ball downfield . Last week against Georgia, this Crimson Tide defense showed some flaws when junior running back Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 120 yards on just 17 carries . That's the same number of carries Bishop averages per game this season, and Alabama is coming off a game where it struggled to stop the run. Bishop is averaging 113 yards per game and more than six yards per carry this season. If he gets his usual workload, he should be in a great spot to record 90-plus rushing yards on Saturday. Prop pick #3: Keelon Russell Over 24.5 Rush Yards (53.49%) I gave out this same prop last week, so I'll start this one the same way: If you can secure Russell's longest rush over 15.5 yards , take it! However, Russell has still rushed for Over 25 yards in four of his six games this season . The sophomore quarterback is averaging 7.66 rushing attempts per game, and with the Crimson Tide likely to be leading, as the spread indicates, they'll eventually want to chew some clock. That should give Russell plenty of chances to rack up yards on the ground. The last mobile quarterback Tennessee faced was Auburn's Byrum Brown, who averages 16.2 rushing attempts per game and racked up more than 107 rushing yards against the Volunteers. away.headline: How can Alabama football receiving corps hold up without Ryan Coleman-Williams?
away.blurb: Coleman-Williams is recovering from arthroscopic surgery and a head injury, with his return status being evaluated week-by-week. "It was a little tougher to get him out there," Grubb said. "He was going like crazy trying to get himself ready. He's a tough kid, but he had that thing wrapped, and we were just a little hesitant on how much he was going to be able to do." Other players, including Cederian Morgan, have also been dealing with injuries, impacting the team's offensive depth. Offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb expressed a desire for other receivers, like Noah Rogers, to get more playing time. Alabama football's offensive performances through the past two weeks have been lackluster, a dread that has been felt in the absence of Ryan Coleman-Williams. Coleman-Williams had arthroscopic surgery to repair a meniscus injury, per ESPN. He also has a head injury suffered in Alabama 's 20-17 loss to Georgia. Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer said Coleman-Williams is one of five players "in the same boat" of being evaluated week-by-week. "Ryan is also – again, all these guys are kind of in the same area, in the same window," DeBoer said. "I would not expect them to be practicing all week long, but, you know, we'll kind of see as the week gets to the end what that looks like." The Crimson Tide totaled 147 receiving yards off of 19 catches in last week's 26-10 loss at Tennessee, dispersed fairly evenly between Rico Scott, Lotzeir Brooks and tight end Marshall Pritchett. Scott led the Crimson Tide with four catches for 54 yards, while sophomore Derek Meadows was what offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb said was the highest workload change among the corps, playing in upwards of 50 snaps. Grubb, however, was not satisfied with the amount of time senior transder Noah Rogers saw the field. "Honestly, when I heard how many snaps he got after the game, I was a little bummed," Grubb said. "Some of that was just due to lack of length of drives, just not being sustainable and staying on the field, poor performance on third down. So that part was a little bit tough." Freshman Cederian Morgan was also nursing a hamstring injury the week leading up to the Tennessee loss. Missing a couple days of practice affected how capable he was of seeing the field. As the Crimson Tide finds itself riddled with injuries deeper into the season, gaps will need to be filled to contribute to a productive offense. Coleman-Williams remains pending, recording 23 catches for 415 yards and four touchdowns through six games so far this season. "It's tough not having Ryan there," Grubb said. "He's such a present and a positive influence on the players, and just a calming kind of guy just to get the guys going a little bit."
