picks.headline: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why?
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Somewhat quietly, one of the bigger games on college football slate this weekend is happening at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium between No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) and No. 13 Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). Both squads enter with one loss and need a win this weekend to maintain a reasonable path to the College Football Playoffs. However, alongside the high-stakes of the matchup are the storylines revolving around each team’s roster. Rebels’ star running back Kewan Lacy will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Missouri, following his true freshman season in 2024. Meanwhile, former Ole Miss starters Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee and Chris Graves Jr. all return to Oxford for the first time since they entered the transfer portal, following the Rebels’ deep run through last year’s playoffs. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 2:30 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the week as six-point home favorites. Ahead of the Rebels' latest pressure-filled matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on after an interception against the Florida Gators during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Welcome to the gauntlet that is the College Football Playoffs….or at least the very real warmup version of it. The loser of this weekend’s game in Oxford isn’t mathematically out of the 12-team race, but it’s going to be a loss that will be immensely hard to overcome looking at Ole Miss’ and Missouri’s schedule. As far as the actual matchup is concerned, going into the game, Missouri has played better on the defensive side of the ball and matches the Rebels’ offensive firepower with Austin Simmons and Jamal Roberts leading the way. The Tigers’ rush attack could have the ability to give the Rebels a long afternoon, and we’ll really find out if Ole Miss improved enough from its nightmare performance defending the run against Florida. Ole Miss doesn’t have to completely shut down Mizzou’s ground game, it more than likely won’t, but if it can limit Roberts and the rest of the production in the backfield, the Rebels should give themselves a real chance at picking up a critical win. In my mind, that’s going to be the key to victory for Ole Miss. I believe this game will come down to the final few possessions and whichever offense has the ball last in that scenario. Given the large sample size we’ve seen of Trinidad Chambliss in those types of situations, I have a hard time picking against those results. Ole Miss 34, Missouri 31 Matt Galatzan All of the talk is going to be about the return of Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee to Oxford, and Kewan Lacy facing off against his former team. However, there needs to be more talk about Missouri's defense, or more specifically, its pass rush. The Tigers have 18 sacks this year, which is tied with Texas for third in the SEC behind LSU and Tennessee. Meanwhile, the Rebels are No. 1 in the SEC in sacks allowed with just five. If the Rebels can protect Trinidad Chambliss and slow down a balanced Missouri offense, they will be in good shape. I think they do both just enough to get the win. Ole Miss 30, Missouri 27 I think Ole Miss will take home a hard-fought victory against former Rebels’ quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and the rest of the Missouri Tigers. Simmons, Lee and running back Jamal Roberts are likely to give head coach Pete Golding and his defense trouble, leading to a “bend-don’t-break” type of performance, following a bounce-back game against Vanderbilt for the Rebels’ defense. However, I’m comfortable predicting Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, wide receiver Deuce Alexander and running back Kewan Lacy to outplay Simmons, Lee and Roberts and give the Rebels a high-scoring ranked win in Ole Miss’ homecoming game. Ole Miss 38, Missouri 31 Zion Trammell Ole Miss and Missouri feature star-studded quarterbacks in Trinidad Chambliss and Austin Simmons. This has the makings of a high-scoring affair, so whichever quarterback can protect the ball better could decide the outcome. I think Chambliss and Kewan Lacy play their best games of the year, and Ole Miss gets by with a win. Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28 Cooper Ferguson Back in the Vaught, I want to see a great response to the blowout victory in Nashville. All will go well if Trinidad Chambliss plays as he has so far. After a second-half respite in the Vanderbilt game, Kewan Lacy is primed for a breakout game in the 2026 campaign. I fear the talent and connection between Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee, but I do not see the Rebels dropping a game at VHS this season. Published Oct 16, 2026 TYLER KOMIS Bio: Tyler Komis is a beat reporter for Ole Miss On SI. He is a Biletnikoff Award and Lombardi Award voter from New Jersey with more than five years of sports reporting experience. Prior to joining On SI, he previously covered Ole Miss Athletics for 247Sports (2021-2026), chronicling the ascension of the football program and the beginning of its coaching transition to Pete Golding ahead of the 2025-26 College Football Playoffs. You can find Komis on social media channels, including X/Twitter @TylerKomis. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Missouri-Ole Miss Winner After Changing His Pick on Air Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Rece Davis expected to be the only voice backing No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss on Saturday, but the College GameDay host changed his prediction after ESPN’s Dan Wetzel and Pete Thamel both took the Tigers first. Davis made his pick on the College GameDay Podcast . He’s forecasting a back-and-forth game in Oxford that ends with the Rebels holding off former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons and the Tigers. Why Rece Davis switched his pick Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) hands the ball off to running back Makhi Frazier (25) against the Vanderbilt Commodores | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis came into the segment leaning toward Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). That’s the same side ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took earlier this week . Davis came into the segment leaning toward Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). That’s the same side ESPN analyst Greg McElroy took earlier this week . “You guys have surprised me because I thought for sure I was going to be the only one to pick Missouri,” Davis said. “I’m going to change my mind a little bit. Not just because you guys took Missouri, but I was leaning Missouri. Austin Simmons’ revenge, running game, the whole thing.” Davis also pointed to Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz, saying “a lot of times when Drink hits the mic, sometimes it doesn’t work out as well for the Tigers.” His forecast echoes Sept. 26, when Missouri gave up a fourth-quarter lead in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. “A back-and-forth game, up and down. Probably ends up much like Missouri’s last trip to the state of Mississippi,” Davis said. “I’ll say the Rebels hang on. I’ll be the one who says the home team wins it.” Missouri’s top-10 history at stake Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Missouri has rolled since that loss. The Tigers routed No. 8 Florida 45-17 , giving Drinkwitz his first regular-season win over a top-10 team in 11 tries at Missouri, and then beat Texas A&M 27-6. Missouri has rolled since that loss. The Tigers routed No. 8 Florida 45-17 , giving Drinkwitz his first regular-season win over a top-10 team in 11 tries at Missouri, and then beat Texas A&M 27-6. “If Missouri can do it, having a top-10 win because the Gators were top 10 at the time, they can win multiple games against top-10 teams for the first time since 1978,” Davis said. That 1978 team shut out defending national champion Notre Dame 3-0 and beat No. 2 Nebraska 35-31. Simmons lost Ole Miss’ starting job after a Week 2 ankle injury against Kentucky in 2025. At Missouri, the left-hander has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns and one interception, which is one yard fewer than Trinidad Chambliss has for the Rebels. Tigers running back Jamal Roberts leads the SEC in rushing. He’ll face an Ole Miss run defense that ranks last in the conference at 176.4 yards allowed per game and 106th nationally in EPA per rush allowed . “The Ole Miss defense hasn’t been what we thought it was going to be,” Davis said. “I remember talking to some people in the preseason, thinking this might be one of the best defensive fronts in college football. Maybe it’ll turn out to be, but so far we haven’t seen evidence of that.” How can Ole Miss hang on? Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) counters with Chambliss, a Heisman Trophy contender who’s back for another season after he won an injunction against the NCAA , and running back Kewan Lacy, who began his career at Missouri. “There’s also a little bit at stake here in the personal rivalry for Trinidad Chambliss, too. Maybe Kewan Lacy,” Davis said. Lacy set Ole Miss’ single-season record with 1,567 rushing yards in 2025 and signed a deal to return to Oxford . Still, his health hangs over this week. A shoulder injury kept him out of the 52-28 loss at Florida, and he left last week’s 52-17 win at Vanderbilt after seven carries. The Rebels’ offense ranks eighth nationally in success rate, while Missouri’s defense has allowed 23 points total across its last two games. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET on SEC Network, and the loser falls to 2-2 in SEC play. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. away.headline: Ex-Rebels lead No. 13 Missouri into Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss

He’s completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. “He’s playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system,” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. home.blurb: Seventeen players remained on Missouri football’s official SEC availability and injury report on Thursday, including a “probable” designation for quarterback Austin Simmons. Two players have been downgraded to "doubtful" to play: starting tight end Brett Norfleet and rotational linebacker Jeremiah Beasley. Two players are "questionable" to play: starting defensive lineman Sterling Webb and starting linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. Seven players are listed as "probable" to play: Starting QB Austin Simmons, starting left tackle Cayden Green, starting wide receiver Cayden Lee, key edge rushers Darris Smith and Daeden Hopkins, starting safety Santana Banner and backup corner Cam Keys. Mizzou, as expected, ruled out running backs Ahmad Hardy and Malae Fonoti, right tackle Josh Atkins, reserve safety JaDon Blair and backup tight end Gavin Hoffman for this weekend's game. The Tigers also downgraded backup right guard Khalief Canty Jr., who is now officially ruled out of playing Ole Miss. Before a 27-6 win over Texas A&M this past Saturday, Mizzou listed 16 players on its midweek availability reports. On gameday, the Tigers removed all 11 players who weren’t previously ruled out, making them eligible to play. picks.headline: Florida State @ Miami Preview And Prediction
picks.blurb: Florida State @ Miami Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Hurts reportedly out for season NFL news, updates Rays take 3-2 ALCS lead NFL Winners and Losers WNBA Finals Game 2 preview Florida State @ Miami Preview And Prediction Oct 3, 2026; Clemson, South Carolina, USA; Miami Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) celebrates a first down during the third quarteragainst the Clemson Tigers at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Ashley Tumlin-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 9:10 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 3 Miami looks unstoppable heading into its rivalry showdown with Florida State. Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. How Each Team Wins For Miami, the formula is simple: establish the run, protect the football, and allow Mensah to attack Florida State's secondary. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. Final Score: No. 3 Miami 45, Florida State 20 Miami remains undefeated, improves to 6-0, and strengthens its national championship case. picks.blurb: Predicting the No. 3 Miami Hurricanes Starter at Right Guard Against Florida State Seminoles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Hurts reportedly out for season NFL news, updates Rays take 3-2 ALCS lead NFL Winners and Losers WNBA Finals Game 2 preview (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Anthony Aguirre Sat, October 17, 2026 at 3:10 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads MIAMI, Fla. – Ahead of Saturday night's in-state rivalry matchup against the Florida State Seminoles , the No. 3 Miami Hurricanes will have a new starting right guard. Sophomore Max Buchanan will be sidelined for an extensive portion of the season. He was injured in the Hurricanes' 41-13 win over Clemson at Death Valley (Memorial Stadium). Despite returning to finish the game, Buchanan underwent surgecal repairs. Given the Hurricanes' cross-training for offensive linemen, head coach Mario Cristobal will have a plethora of options. The big question: Who does he trust the most? It won't be revealed until kickoff, but here are candidates looking to take the starting role, plus a final prediction. After Buchanan initially went down against the Tigers, it was the fellow sophomore who stepped in. Alofaituli lost his starting role at left guard to freshman Max Buchanan. The 21-year-old logged 32 offensive snaps and finished with a 55 pass-protection Pro Football Focus grade. However, Alofaituli didn't allow a sack, pressure, hit, or hurry. He played the entirety of the Hurricanes' nine-play touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, which they exclusively ran the ball. However, Alofaituli doesn't have the traditional size for a guard. He's listed at 6-2 and 298 pounds. It's proven to be a weakness at times and the Seminoles could exploit if Alofaituli is lined up at right guard. It's been a slow freshman campaign for the former elite five-star recruit. Cantwell has logged just 78 offensive snaps through five games. As both starting tackle roles are occupied by veterans Samson Okunlola (left) and Matthew McCoy (right), the only real opportunities for the 18-year-old to play is in the interior. Cantwell has 59 snaps at right guard, but carving out a rotational role has been a different challenge. The Nixa (Mo.) native will very likely play at tackle as early as next season, but right guard is currently up for grabs. Cantwell could seize the moment, unless this final candidate has something to say about it. The Georgia transfer joined the Coral Gables program with experience all over the line of scrimmage, except center. Meriweather has played in a reserve role, but could be the closest to climbing the depth chart. In the Hurricanes' 52-3 win over Central Michigan, he logged 28 snaps and all were at right guard. Both programs are powerhouses and multiple National Championship winners, but it's different this time around. The Seminoles have progressively declined since the 2023 13-1 season; meanwhile, the Hurricanes are on the brink of fully reclaiming former glory. Here is what's most important to know before Saturday night's game: Television Channel: ESPN Kickoff Time: 7:00 p.m. E.T. The Hurricanes are -2000 favorites to win and the Seminoles have a +1000 chance to pull off an upset. The spread is at -20.5 and the over/under is at 50.5. The following Hurricanes players are ruled out: Wide receiver Joshua Moore (Upper-Body; Out for Season), running back CharMar "Marty" Brown (Left Leg; Out for Season), cornerback Ja'Boree Antoine (Undisclosed), right guard Max Buchanan (Left Knee), cornerback Romans "OJ" Frederique Jr. (Left Shoulder), and tight end Luka Gilbert (Undisclosed; Out for Season). Junior cornerback Xavier Lucas is set to return from a four-game absence. Star edge rusher Marquise Lightfoot, linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr., and cornerback Damari Brown were banged up ahead of the bye week, but aren't listed on the injury report. The following Seminoles are ruled out: Running back Samuel Singleton Jr., wide receiver Devin Carter, safety Karson Hobbs, linebacker Blake Nichelson, cornerback Jamari Howard, linebacker Izayia Williams, cornerback Jordan Crutchfield, and linebacker Daylen Green. Freshman linebacker Noah LaValle was listed as questionable on the initial injury report, but has been officially ruled out. Meanwhile, edge rusher Darryll Desir and center Paul Bowling are probable. The Hurricanes will likely look to force Daniels to throw more while simultaneously stopping the run – a similar game plan against Clemson and freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds. However, where Daniels lacks in passing, the 22-year-old makes up for on the gound. He leads the ACC with 10 rushing touchdowns. Defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman has a fair amount of experience in facing dual-threat quarterbacks and finding success. The Hurricanes have the highest-scoring offense (averaging 49.6 points) in FBS; meanwhile, the Seminoles have the 20th worst total defense. It should be a lopsided matchup at Hard Rock Stadium, but rivalrly games can get interesting. You could argue that the biggest surprise of the college football campaign is that Mike Norvell is still employed by Florida State . The shouts for Norvell's axing are likely to get louder this week as the Seminoles travel to No. 3 Miami as 21.5-point underdogs before hitting their bye week. If Florida State is blown out for the second straight week, it could be curtains for Norvell. It is almost certainly delaying the inevitable, but I think the Seminoles may be able to avoid getting embarrassed at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday. I'm not saying that Florida State will win, or even make Miami sweat it out, but the Seminoles are competent enough to keep this thing within three scores. It's a low bar, I know. away.headline: Miami vs Florida State live updates: Hurricanes, Seminoles head to OT
away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: Ashton Daniels kneeled out the clock, and we're headed to overtime. The teams will alternate possessions starting at the opponents' 25-yard line. If it goes to a second overtime, teams will have to go for 2 if they score a touchdown. After that, the teams will trade 2-point conversion tries until there's a winner. In his first game back since the opener at Stanford, cornerback Xavier Lucas made what could turn out to be the biggest play of the game. Tre Wisner got loose on a long run, but Ethan O'Connor stripped the ball loose, sending the ball skidding across the wet grass. Lucas fell on it to give Miami the ball at its own 39. Darian Mensah may not be having his best game, but he is still showing impeccable touch on some difficult throws. He got a throw out just before Rylan Kennedy could get to him, lofting a 19-yard looper to Vandrevius Jacobs. As the fourth quarter begins, the Canes have the ball at the FSU 20. Miami outgained FSU 149-76 in the third quarter, but the visitors benefitted big time on two turnovers (one on downs). UM can't afford to miss here if they want to stay undefeated. One play after Ousmane Kromah was carted to the locker room with a devastating ankle injury, Ashton Daniels took it in himself for the game-tying touchdown from 2 yards out. He held up three and two fingers to shout out Kromah's number 32 after the score. With FSU driving again and the 2-minute timeout having just passed, Chase Smith wrapped up Ousmane Kromah by the ankles. The running back was injured on the play, and trainers brought out an air cast for him. He was carted off the field. The Seminoles were already without Sam Singleton Jr. entering the game; without Kromah, among the top-20 running backs in the nation with 565 yards entering the game, Texas transfer Tre Wisner becomes their main RB. After a Miami three-and-out, Ashton Daniels returned to the game and looked like he didn't miss a beat, scrambling for 10 yards on a third-and-8. Later, he dumped a screen pass over three rushing Hurricanes to tight end Dessirio Riles for a 23-yard touchdown to tie it up. FSU is averaging 6.1 yards per play against a banged-up Miami defense. Ashton Daniels scrambled for 14 yards. As he slid, safety Zechariah Poyser hit him in the head area, bringing out a flag for the personal foul. His ejection for targeting was upheld upon review. That play and Bryce Fitzgerald's injury leaves an already depleted Miami secondary without two more starters. Xavier Lucas got injured in the opener vs. Stanford and hasn't played since, but he's expected to be back in the starting lineup tonight. O.J. Frederique also has been out since Week 1 but needs more time to return, leaving either Damari Brown, Ethan O'Connor or converted safety Bryce Fitzgerald starting opposite Lucas against FSU. home.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
home.blurb: Ashton Daniels kneeled out the clock, and we're headed to overtime. The teams will alternate possessions starting at the opponents' 25-yard line. If it goes to a second overtime, teams will have to go for 2 if they score a touchdown. After that, the teams will trade 2-point conversion tries until there's a winner. In his first game back since the opener at Stanford, cornerback Xavier Lucas made what could turn out to be the biggest play of the game. Tre Wisner got loose on a long run, but Ethan O'Connor stripped the ball loose, sending the ball skidding across the wet grass. Lucas fell on it to give Miami the ball at its own 39. Darian Mensah may not be having his best game, but he is still showing impeccable touch on some difficult throws. He got a throw out just before Rylan Kennedy could get to him, lofting a 19-yard looper to Vandrevius Jacobs. As the fourth quarter begins, the Canes have the ball at the FSU 20. Miami outgained FSU 149-76 in the third quarter, but the visitors benefitted big time on two turnovers (one on downs). UM can't afford to miss here if they want to stay undefeated. One play after Ousmane Kromah was carted to the locker room with a devastating ankle injury, Ashton Daniels took it in himself for the game-tying touchdown from 2 yards out. He held up three and two fingers to shout out Kromah's number 32 after the score. With FSU driving again and the 2-minute timeout having just passed, Chase Smith wrapped up Ousmane Kromah by the ankles. The running back was injured on the play, and trainers brought out an air cast for him. He was carted off the field. The Seminoles were already without Sam Singleton Jr. entering the game; without Kromah, among the top-20 running backs in the nation with 565 yards entering the game, Texas transfer Tre Wisner becomes their main RB. After a Miami three-and-out, Ashton Daniels returned to the game and looked like he didn't miss a beat, scrambling for 10 yards on a third-and-8. Later, he dumped a screen pass over three rushing Hurricanes to tight end Dessirio Riles for a 23-yard touchdown to tie it up. FSU is averaging 6.1 yards per play against a banged-up Miami defense. Ashton Daniels scrambled for 14 yards. As he slid, safety Zechariah Poyser hit him in the head area, bringing out a flag for the personal foul. His ejection for targeting was upheld upon review. That play and Bryce Fitzgerald's injury leaves an already depleted Miami secondary without two more starters. Xavier Lucas got injured in the opener vs. Stanford and hasn't played since, but he's expected to be back in the starting lineup tonight. O.J. Frederique also has been out since Week 1 but needs more time to return, leaving either Damari Brown, Ethan O'Connor or converted safety Bryce Fitzgerald starting opposite Lucas against FSU. Two teams coming off massive upset victories will collide Saturday night as No. 15 Kentucky (5-1) travels to Norman to face Oklahoma (3-2) in a crucial SEC matchup. Kentucky is coming off a thrilling 35-34 overtime victory over LSU, while Oklahoma stunned Texas 27-24 in the Red River Rivalry. Both programs have plenty to prove, but the biggest question is whether Oklahoma can build on its impressive victory and finally establish some consistency. Kentucky: Can the Wildcats Keep Rolling? Kentucky has been one of the SEC's biggest surprises under first-year head coach Will Stein. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has thrown for 1,394 yards and 11 touchdowns, while running back CJ Baxter has rushed for 484 yards and eight scores. Baxter was outstanding against LSU, rushing for 123 yards and two touchdowns. The Wildcats are averaging nearly 35 points per game, but Oklahoma's defense presents a completely different challenge. Brent Venables has built one of the nation's most physical defensive units, allowing just 17.6 points and approximately 267 yards per game. If Kentucky cannot establish Baxter early, Minchey could face constant pressure throughout the evening. Oklahoma: The Defense Is Carrying This Team Oklahoma's victory over Texas was impressive, but the Sooners still have serious offensive concerns. Quarterback John Mateer has thrown for 1,038 yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Against Texas, Mateer managed just 155 passing yards, and Oklahoma needed a blocked punt touchdown and multiple defensive stops to secure the victory. However, the Sooners' defense has been outstanding. Oklahoma is allowing just 150 passing yards per game, making life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. With Adepoju Adebawore creating pressure up front, the Sooners have the personnel to disrupt Kentucky's offense. If Mateer can avoid turnovers and Oklahoma establishes any consistency running the football, the Sooners should have enough offensive production to win. How Each Team Wins Kentucky must establish Baxter early, protect Minchey, and avoid giving Oklahoma short fields through turnovers. The Wildcats also need to force Mateer into obvious passing situations. For Oklahoma, everything starts defensively. The Sooners must contain Baxter, pressure Minchey, and create opportunities for their offense. Playing in Norman should also provide a significant advantage for Venables' team. I expect Kentucky to keep this game competitive, but Oklahoma's defense will ultimately make the difference. The Wildcats should find some success moving the football, particularly early, but sustaining long drives against this Sooners defense will be extremely difficult. Mateer won't need to deliver a spectacular performance. Instead, Oklahoma will rely on its defense, field position, and a few explosive offensive plays. Expect Kentucky to threaten late before Oklahoma comes up with one final defensive stop. Final Score: Oklahoma 27, No. 15 Kentucky 21 The Sooners build on their Red River victory, improve to 4-2, and keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Sooners host No. 15/17 Kentucky on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. in Norman, and the setup could not be much cleaner for a measuring-stick home opener in SEC play. Oklahoma is 3-2 and 1-1 after knocking off No. 1 Texas on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky is 5-1 and 3-1 after beating No. 10 LSU in overtime. Both teams are coming in hot. Only one of them gets to leave Norman still feeling like the week actually changed something. That is the whole tone of this game. Oklahoma does not need another moral victory. It already got the statement result in the Cotton Bowl. Now the question is whether Brent Venables ' team can stack a second one against a ranked opponent at home, in throwbacks, with the building expecting the version of the Sooners that showed up after halftime in Dallas. The storyline writes itself. Oklahoma just beat the top team in the country. Kentucky just survived LSU 35-34 in overtime for its second straight 35-34 overtime win. Will Stein's group is not sneaking into Norman quietly. This is Kentucky's highest AP ranking since 2022, and the Wildcats are playing with the kind of confidence that makes road environments less intimidating than they used to be. Stein's background adds a little spice too. He was on Texas' staff from 2015 to 2017, then spent the last three years as Oregon's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach while the Ducks made the College Football Playoff. He knows big stages. More importantly for Saturday, he has a quarterback in Kenny Minchey who takes care of the ball, extends plays, and has already shown he can finish tight games. Oklahom a's recent history after Texas also hangs over the night. Since 1999, the Sooners are 25-2 in the game immediately following the Red River rivalry. The only losses in that stretch were to Kansas State in 2014 and South Carolina in 2024. That is a real trend, but trends do not tackle Minchey or cover Kentucky's skill players. Oklahoma still has to earn the next one. If the Sooners are going to control this game, it starts where most of their best football has started all year: on defense. Oklahoma is allowing just 12.8 first downs per game, best in the country. The Sooners also rank among the national leaders in third-down defense, red-zone defense, passing defense, total defense, and sacks. Opponents have scored on only 15 of 62 possessions. The second-half numbers are even tighter. Oklahoma has given up just 27 points after halftime all season, including only three in the third quarter. That profile matters against a quarterback like Minchey. He is efficient, hard to rattle, and dangerous when the pocket breaks down. Oklahoma cannot afford soft edges or impatient linebackers. The formula is the same one that showed up against Texas: keep contain, force longer developing throws, win early downs, and make Kentucky drive the hard way. The Sooners are 11-2 under Venables when they score a defensive touchdown, including 4-0 since the start of last season. They do not need another pick-six Saturday. They do need the same disruptive identity. The personnel is built for it too. All 14 defensive starters began their college careers at Oklahoma. Owen Heinecke has been the tone-setter again, leading the team in tackles in four of five games. Peyton Bowen just took over a rivalry game. Courtland Guillory made the late interception that set up the Texas winner. The front still has Taylor Wein, David Stone, Danny Okoye, and enough depth to keep the pressure coming. If that group plays clean, Oklahoma has a real chance to dictate the night. The uncomfortable truth is that Oklahoma's offense is still looking for consistency even after the biggest win of the season. The Texas game gave the Sooners a blueprint more than a finished product. They scored in all three phases, finally got some second-half juice on the ground through Lloyd Avant, and did just enough in the passing game when the moment arrived. John Mateer did not have to play hero ball. Isaiah Sategna still created the biggest throws on the final drive. Rocky Beers continues to look like one of the smarter portal additions on the roster, ranking among the national leaders in receiving yards per game by a tight end. That is the version Oklahoma needs again. Not perfect. Just complementary. The red-zone efficiency has been solid, and the explosive pass plays are still there. What has lagged is the ability to stay on schedule without leaning so hard on the defense and special teams. Kentucky's defense has not been elite by the numbers, but Venables already made clear that "relief" is not the word inside the building. Every week is still about Oklahoma getting better. The offensive line remains one of the quieter swing factors. Michael Fasusi has been working back from the shoulder injury that knocked him out after the opener, and any step toward getting the line more whole helps the whole operation. Avant gave the run game a pulse against Texas. Xavier Robinson and Tory Blaylock still have to become more reliable pieces if Oklahoma wants drives that do not feel like they are always one negative play from stalling. There are plenty of side notes around the game, and most of them favor the home team if Oklahoma plays like it should. The Sooners are wearing the Bud Wilkinson-era throwbacks again. Memorial Stadium has been a fortress since 1999, with a 153-17 record and a sellout streak that never seems to blink. Venables is 2-2 in conference home openers. The roster has true veteran captains across both sides of the ball. Special teams, once a liability, now look like a genuine strength with Tate Sandell , Grayson Miller, and Doug Deakin's unit playing with confidence. But the schedule context is what keeps this from feeling comfortable. Oklahoma has already seen Michigan, Georgia, and Texas. Still left are Kentucky, Mississippi State, Ole Miss, and Missouri among the ranked or dangerous remaining names. This is not a soft landing after Dallas. It is the next hard one. Kentucky is good enough to punish a flat home team, especially if Minchey gets into a rhythm and Oklahoma's offense stalls early. That is why Saturday matters beyond one week in the standings. The Texas win stopped the spiral and put Oklahoma back in the conversation. A home win over a ranked Kentucky team would make that conversation real. A letdown would turn Dallas back into an isolated highlight instead of the start of a run. The Sooners do not need to look perfect. They need to look intentional. Defend with the same edge that has carried them all year. Run the ball well enough to keep the game clean. Let Mateer manage instead of force. Protect the edges against Minchey. And finish the night like a team that understands the standard is no longer just competing in these games. Oklahoma has the defense. It has the home field. It has the momentum. Kentucky has the confidence of a team that has already won a couple of ugly, important games. Saturday night in Norman should tell us which one is actually building something.

picks.headline: No. 15 Kentucky at Oklahoma: KSR Staff Predictions
Kentucky Wildcats at Oklahoma Sooners Prediction, Picks & Odds for Week 7
How No. 15 Kentucky football & Oklahoma match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Having led Kentucky to back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins, Kenny Minchey is proving himself a cool customer under game-deciding stress. Two weeks ago at South Carolina, Minchey had running back CJ Baxter make a pre-snap shift so he could pick up an otherwise-free edge rusher. As the block was achieved, Minchey threw the game-winning two-point-conversion pass. Last week, Minchey realized the LSU defense had a Grand Canyon-sized hole in the middle of its formation. On a called pass play, the Hendersonville, Tennessee, product instead ran right through that hole for the game-winning two-point-conversion run. On the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey is completing 67.4% of his passes and has thrown for 1,394 yards with 11 touchdown throws vs. one interception. • Oklahoma’s John Mateer began the season on the outskirts of the Heisman Trophy discussion but has so far had a rough go in 2026. Ball security has been a problem for the 6-1, 224-pound Mateer. He threw a crucial interception late in Oklahoma’s 17-10 loss at Michigan in Week 2. He also turned the ball over three times in the first half at Georgia on Sept. 26, helping the Bulldogs open a 28-0 halftime lead en route to a 41-13 win. In Oklahoma’s 27-24 upset of then-No. 1 Texas last week, however, Mateer completed 18 of 26 passes for 155 yards with no interceptions. Mateer has not been as effective a rusher so far in 2026 as he has been in past seasons. Through five games, Mateer has a net-70 yards rushing. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky’s CJ Baxter ripped off a 77-yard run on UK’s first play from scrimmage in last week’s win over LSU. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, finished with 123 rushing yards on 19 carries against the Tigers. A transfer from Texas, Baxter is fifth in the SEC in rushing with 484 yards. Third-year player Jason Patterson has carried only seven times combined in the past two games after suffering an apparent injury at South Carolina. A 5-10, 204-pound product of Sneads, Florida, Patterson had been one of UK’s breakout players over the season’s first four games. • Oklahoma’s ground game has, so far, been mostly stalled. The Sooners are last in the SEC in rushing, averaging only 95.8 yards a game. Lloyd Avant Jr ., a transfer from Colorado State who began his college career at Tulsa, leads the Sooners in rushing with 239 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries (an average of 4.5 yards a rush). Avant, however, had a strong showing in the win over Texas, rushing 10 times for 72 yards and a touchdown. Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby was named SEC Freshman of the Week for the second straight week after catching four passes for 79 yards, including two crucial receptions late in the game, in the win over LSU. On the season, Darby, a 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, is eighth in the SEC in receptions (29) and ninth in receiving yards (401). Ja’Kayden Ferguson had caught only three total passes in UK’s first five games, but the 6-2, 184-pound, second-year player made three key receptions in the win over LSU. “He made some unbelievable plays,” Will Stein said of Ferguson. “... He blocked hard. He played hard. He’s got a lot of talent, a lot of upside.” • Isaiah Sategna III has been Oklahoma’s most effective offensive skill player so far in 2026. The 5-10, 185-pound senior from Austin, Texas, has 25 catches for 331 yards and two touchdowns. Sategna caught five passes for 64 yards in the win over Texas. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez made a team-high six catches for 25 yards vs. LSU. A 6-4, 249-pound junior from Covington Catholic, Rodriguez is second on the UK team in receptions (28) and receiving yards (219). Henry Boyer had a quiet showing vs. LSU with one catch for four yards. The 6-6, 270-pound transfer from Illinois has only nine catches on the season, but those receptions have yielded 120 receiving yards and three touchdowns. • Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers is, like UK’s Rodriguez, one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. A 6-5, 240-pound senior from Littleton, Colorado, Beers has 22 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Beers had four catches for 29 yards vs. Texas. Hayden Hansen caught 30 passes for 254 yards and two TDs last season while playing for Florida. So far this season, the 6-8, 270-pound Hansen has five catches for 74 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even Offensive line • After having a rough go against Alabama in Week 2, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has consistently been playing solid football. “Malachi is a really-good football player,” Will Stein said. “The guy is 6-8, 330 pounds. He is gonna be, probably, a top three-round NFL draft pick in the next couple years. “ • The Oklahoma offensive front has been much-criticized amidst the Sooners’ offensive struggles, but the unit showed some signs of hope in the second half vs. Texas. Freshman Noah Best has emerged as the jack-of-all-trades on the OU offensive line, already logging starts this season at center and both guard positions. Defensive line • Kentucky nose guard Jamarrion Harkless was one of the unsung heroes of the win over LSU. The 6-3, 346-pound alumnus of Frederick Douglass High School made three tackles, 1.5 sacks, forced a fumble and had a quarterback hurry against Lane Kiffin’s Tigers. “I told (Harkless) ‘That’s how you have to play for us to be successful on defense, game in, game out,’” Will Stein said. • Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone is an interior force. The 6-3, 312-pound junior from Del City, Oklahoma, made five tackles in the win over Texas. On the season, Stone has 19 tackles, two tackles for loss and half a sack. Advantage : Oklahoma • Due to injuries, Kentucky starting linebackers Grant Godfrey and Bo Barnes had to be iron men vs. LSU. WLB Barnes made 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss, while MLB Godfrey made 10 stops vs. the Tigers. • Oklahoma MLB Owen Heinecke leads the Sooners in tackles (36), is tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (two) and is second in tackles for loss (4.5). A 6-1, 226-pound fifth-year player from Tulsa, Heinecke made nine tackles vs. Texas. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior strong safety Ty Bryant made six tackles and intercepted a pass vs. LSU. For the 6-foot, 196-pound Bryant, a product of Frederick Douglass High School, it was his sixth career pick. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols made seven tackles and successfully defended a pass vs. LSU. • Oklahoma strong safety Peyton Bowen returned an interception of Texas quarterback Arch Manning 42 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter last week. A 6-foot, 200-pound product of Corinth, Texas, Bowen has made 24 tackles on the season, leads the Sooners in pass breakups with four and also has a forced fumble and a sack. Special teams • Kentucky punt returner Brock Coffman brought an LSU kick back 55 yards for a touchdown last week. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui entered last week’s game 6 of 7 on field-goal attempts but went only 2 of 4 vs. LSU. However, after missing two makeable field goals in the fourth quarter last week, Zouagui came back to hit a 33-yard field goal with 12 seconds left in the contest to tie the game at 27 and force overtime. After Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara punted in UK’s first five games, the Cats turned to former starter Wilson Berry vs. LSU. On three punts, Berry averaged 40.1 yards and pinned LSU inside its 20-yard line once. • Oklahoma’s special teams are elite. Danny Okoye blocked a Texas punt last week that Dakoda Fields recovered in the Longhorns’ end zone for a touchdown. Isaiah Sategna III is second in the SEC in punt returning, averaging 18.57 yards a return. He had an 88-yard punt-return touchdown in the season opener vs. UTEP. Punter Jacob Ulrich is averaging 44.31 yards on 16 kicks and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line three times. Place-kicker Tate Sandell kicked a 47-yard field goal on the game’s final play to beat Texas last week. On the season, Sandell is 5 of 8 on field goals with a long make of 53 yards (which also came against Texas). picks.headline: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Kentucky Wildcats final score predictions: Can the Sooners get back in the CFP discussion with a win?
picks.blurb: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Kentucky Wildcats final score predictions: Can the Sooners get back in the CFP discussion with a win? Skip to content NFL Close Menu All NFL Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks College Football Close Menu All College Football Alabama Crimson Tide Auburn Tigers Florida Gators Georgia Bulldogs Miami Hurricanes Michigan Wolverines Notre Dame Fighting Irish Ohio State Buckeyes Oklahoma Sooners Ole Miss Rebels Penn State Nittany Lions Tennessee Volunteers Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Draft Simulator Trade Simulator Toggle Mobile Navigation Home College Football The Oklahoma Sooners will host a strong Kentucky Wildcats team on Saturday night. The Oklahoma Sooners are coming off of a huge win over the Texas Longhorns at the Cotton Bowl in the Red River Rivalry. The Kentucky Wildcats are coming off a huge overtime win over LSU. Both teams are on a high but are looking to improve their records on Saturday night. So, does the team in Kentucky that's maybe at its best as a program get the win? Or does Oklahoma get another ranked win and get back into the College Football Playoff conversation? Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Oklahoma 20, Kentucky 17 This feels almost like the clock striking midnight for Kentucky here, as much as it does for me, who's lived the last two weeks dangerously. Both teams are coming in off super highs from last week. Oklahoma clipped Texas 27-24 on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky walked off LSU 35-34 in overtime, their second straight walk-off overtime win, going for two and getting it on the final play. Honestly, in a vacuum, I trust Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey more than I trust OU's John Mateer. But Minchey is going up against a very good Oklahoma defense, while Mateer has a more navigable task when he has the ball. I still don't see points a plenty here, but Oklahoma forces a key turnover late, and that's enough with the home crowd in Norman to get a close and resume-boosting win at the season's midpoint. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 20 This could be one of the ugliest games on the schedule, with both teams struggling to find much offensive consistency. Oklahoma will have chances to pull away, but John Mateer’s chaotic style makes it hard to trust the Sooners to put together four clean quarters. Mateer can make spectacular plays, but mistakes and questionable decisions could give Kentucky the extra possessions it needs to hang around. Don't expect a shootout here. This game could come down to which team makes fewer costly mistakes in the fourth quarter. I'm buying a little bit of Kentucky magic in this one. Kenny Minchey comes through with a couple of clutch plays at the biggest moments, giving the Wildcats just enough offense to pull off a road upset. Kentucky might not look dominant, and it certainly won't be pretty, but this team finds a way to make things interesting when the game is on the line. Oklahoma has a chance to put the Wildcats away but can't quite finish the job, opening the door for Kentucky to steal a win in a close, low-scoring battle. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 16 Will Stein has the Wildcats on a heater right now, and he's doing it with the two things you want in Kentucky's place: confidence and guts. He's won two games this season because the Wildcats went for two at the end, and that kind of belief in your team will go a long way in establishing a foundation for your program. Things are different for the Sooners, who are coming off of a fantastic win in Red River. Even so, John Mateer can't do much other than throw shock, and he did that brilliantly on the final drive against Texas. I don't think Mateer will change overnight, and the Wildcats will take advantage of him enough to win. Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 14 This game suddenly looks much better than it did a week ago after both Kentucky and Oklahoma pulled off massive upsets last weekend. Red River can always get wonky, but few expected OU to beat the number one team in the nation given how the offense has played. Will Stein's Wildcats have gone from quietly looking like a good football team to potentially being one of the conference's better teams after just one loss to Alabama and a last-minute OT win over LSU. The truth, however, is that OU may have found something more than just some Red River magic. This will be arguably the hardest test of the year for Kenny Minchey, and the battle of the brains between Brent Venables and Will Stein will be notable, but I think Oklahoma will get the job done. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 17 The Oklahoma Sooners are almost ready to kick off their first SEC night game (excluding CFP games) since 2024. And this one should be big, with both teams riding an insane high after huge wins. The Kentucky Wildcats will give OU's defense fits. It will happen, and I know my score prediction probably doesn't show that, but I have OU getting a few takeaways in this one. Kentucky is going to do a bunch of pre-snap stuff that's going to confuse you. They are very good at that, but Brent Venables has his unit locked in right now. OU will win this game once again through the defense and special teams, with some little moments here and there from the offense. away.headline: Mailbag: How will CJ Baxter, other injuries affect Kentucky's playoff outlook?
away.blurb: Baxter was listed as a game-time decision on the pre-Oklahoma availability report. He participated in warmups and was running sprints on the sideline throughout the game but didn’t actually play. If Baxter does experience any setbacks this week, it does feel like holding him out against Vanderbilt with a bye week to follow would be a wise choice since Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes can still carry the load at running back. Vanderbilt is winless in SEC play, but Kentucky must still be on alert this week. This team needs a bye week to rest a variety of injuries, but I would be wary about holding anyone out against the Commodores who can play at other positions with less depth. The linebacker depth should be helped by the return of Alex Afari, but he did not play in Oklahoma, even after a judge made him eligible on Friday. The injuries for backup linebacker Antwan Smith and backup nickel back Jaden Smith appear to be long-term issues, so do not expect them back soon. Wide receiver Nic Anderson’s status will be worth watching this week too after he appeared to reaggravate his arm/shoulder issue in Oklahoma. For most of the history of Kentucky football winning in the home stadium of a traditional power like Oklahoma would have been the high point of a season. But for this Kentucky team, it wasn’t even the highlight of the month. Kentucky rode its opportunistic defense to a 21-13 win over Oklahoma to move to 6-1 on the season and 4-1 in SEC play. The No. 12 Wildcats are tied for first place in the SEC and seem likely to be slotted in a projected playoff spot when the committee releases its first ranking on Nov. 3, as long as Will Stein’s team takes care of business against Vanderbilt this week. Regardless of what happens from here, Stein has given Big Blue Nation reason to dream. The Wildcats are already bowl eligible, and that fact seems like an afterthought because of bigger goals in reach. Those bigger goals mean fans might not be simply content to ride the current high. To reach the playoff - and contend there - more improvements are needed. That balance is evident in this week’s UK football mailbag. You can submit questions each week via Twitter, Blue Sky or email. Waco Kid on X: Is this real life? What dimension did we magically travel into? When Kentucky was 7-1 in 2018 with a winner-take-all-game for the SEC East against Georgia looming, the playoff only included four teams. It still didn’t feel like Kentucky had a shot to be included in the field. When Kentucky was 6-1 in 2007 with two top-10 wins on the resume and College GameDay headed to Lexington for the first time in program history, there was no playoff. Now, he was in clear pain. “I just listen to the trainers and him, what he’s telling them,” Venables said. “Some guys try to battle through that because they’re able to. He did all he could. If the trainers come over and say somebody’s out or somebody’s up, it goes according to what they say.” “That's just football,” offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said of the offensive line. “We had opportunities there at the end of the game to go win the football game, and I got to be better in those moments and those situations, putting those guys in a position to be successful, regardless of who's out there. “Whatever 11 we have out there, it is my sole responsibility to put those kids in position to go be successful,” Arbuckle said. “Move the ball down the field, capitalize in those situations, those opportunities, regardless of who was out there. I have to be really good about putting those guys in position to go make the plays, to win the football game. NORMAN — Around the midpoint of the third quarter, Ryan Fodje was hurt. Clearly in pain, the second-year Oklahoma offensive lineman limped off the field. Already down three linemen, the training staff re-taped Fodje’s right leg on the sideline and he was back in the game shortly afterward. The Sooners’ offensive line , which held its own for most of Saturday night, unraveled late. Fodje, who struggled to move, allowed two sacks on a critical drive early in the fourth quarter. OU’s offensive line injuries and lack of depth was its fatal flaw in a 21-13 loss to No. 17 Kentucky in which the Sooners outplayed the Wildcats for almost three quarters. With the loss, OU fell to 3-3. TAKEAWAYS: OU football offensive line collapses late in loss vs Kentucky. Can Sooners get healthy? OU finally pulled Fodje late, placing Peyton Joseph at left tackle. Venables was asked postgame about the decision to continue playing Fodje even though he was clearly not 100%. away.blurb: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma Injury Report: CJ Baxter questionable; Michael Fasusi doubtful | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 19, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed The final injury report is out as Kentucky Football gets set for a Saturday night showdown with the Oklahoma Sooners For Kentucky, the big news is linebacker Alex Afari is now eligible again and is expected to play Saturday night . Afari was listed as questionable on the previous two injury reports this week, but he’s no longer on the report, so he’s good to go. As for running back CJ Baxter, he is still listed as questionable. Pete Nakos reported on Friday that Baxter would be a true game-time decision, but there was some optimism on UK’s side that the Texas transfer will play. Defensive tackle Kellan Edwards remains questionable, as does reserve tight end Elijah Brown. Wide receiver Nic Anderson and cornerback Hasaan Sykes are no longer on the injury report after being previously listed as probable. home.blurb: "We had plenty of opportunities there late into the third quarter to knock them out. We just weren't able to get it done.” With Michael Fasusi, Heath Ozaeta and Eddy Pierre-Louis out due to injury, Fodje was already playing out of position on a line filled with backups. Now, he was in clear pain. “I just listen to the trainers and him, what he’s telling them,” Venables said. “Some guys try to battle through that because they’re able to. He did all he could. If the trainers come over and say somebody’s out or somebody’s up, it goes according to what they say.” “That's just football,” offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said of the offensive line. “We had opportunities there at the end of the game to go win the football game, and I got to be better in those moments and those situations, putting those guys in a position to be successful, regardless of who's out there. “Whatever 11 we have out there, it is my sole responsibility to put those kids in position to go be successful,” Arbuckle said. “Move the ball down the field, capitalize in those situations, those opportunities, regardless of who was out there. I have to be really good about putting those guys in position to go make the plays, to win the football game. NORMAN — Around the midpoint of the third quarter, Ryan Fodje was hurt. Clearly in pain, the second-year Oklahoma offensive lineman limped off the field. Already down three linemen, the training staff re-taped Fodje’s right leg on the sideline and he was back in the game shortly afterward. The Sooners’ offensive line , which held its own for most of Saturday night, unraveled late. Fodje, who struggled to move, allowed two sacks on a critical drive early in the fourth quarter. OU’s offensive line injuries and lack of depth was its fatal flaw in a 21-13 loss to No. 17 Kentucky in which the Sooners outplayed the Wildcats for almost three quarters. With the loss, OU fell to 3-3. TAKEAWAYS: OU football offensive line collapses late in loss vs Kentucky. Can Sooners get healthy? The Sooners outgained Kentucky 346-230 but their offense failed to move the ball with any efficiency late due to a decimated offensive line and overall inconsistent decisions. “They made the plays when they needed to, and we weren't able to get it done as a staff or as a team,” said Sooners coach Brent Venables, who is now 58 games into his tenure in which offensive dilemmas are a common theme. OU finally pulled Fodje late, placing Peyton Joseph at left tackle. Venables was asked postgame about the decision to continue playing Fodje even though he was clearly not 100%. The alarming number of injuries on the offensive line and the lack of development under position coach Bill Bedenbaugh in recent years are not new talking points. picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Published Oct 14, 2026 ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! Now the Huskers travel up to Oregon for a 10 p.m. CT matchup, the latest start time for Nebraska since 2014. But other factors in this game make this clash all the more questionable. Dante Moore is out for the game, meaning Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas or even Akili Smith Jr. will be earning the start. But Raiola is the most poetic option after all and is likely the starter despite a rough outing against UCLA. After going 19-of-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, Raiola only threw 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions against the Bruins . He also got strip-sacked in the game. Though it was Raiola's only sack, UCLA still brought the pressure throughout. Raiola's main weakness is pressure, which the Bruins exploited last week. Though Raiola can find ways to stay alive in the pocket and deliver big plays, he rarely takes off downfield and has found himself in rough spots. Thomas took over in the fourth quarter for the Ducks and went 11-of-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown. He did, however, fumble on his opening drive but nearly completed the comeback. But even if Thomas starts, it remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success, especially after seeing Raiola's two-game stretch. Now, Nebraska can get to the quarterback, but the concern comes down to the explosive plays. Indiana pulled off multiple explosive plays last week, despite its struggle to produce points and yardage for most of the game. The Ducks can do the same, especially late in the game. Nebraska ran out of steam in the fourth against Indiana at home early in the afternoon. Now, the Huskers face Oregon on the road after dark. The Ducks almost completed their 17-6 comeback against UCLA, so they can find a way to do the same against Nebraska if needed. The Huskers' defense also needs to be cautious with Oregon's rushing game. Though the Ducks don't strike primarily on the ground, Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison combined for 216 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 54 carries over the last two games, averaging four yards per carry. Though UCLA did suffocate Oregon's run at times, Nebraska could let a play slip by if it's not careful. Oregon's defense also needs to be cautious, seeing how its last two games panned out. The Ducks held USC to 27 points, but Jayden Maiava still threw for 326 yards and two touchdowns on just 23 completions. Oregon also surrendered 205 passing yards on just 13 completions to UCLA, despite holding it to 17 points. Nebraska could do some damage on the run, however. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker tallied 109 rushing yards earlier this season against the Ducks. Anthony Colandrea could do the same and help the Huskers score. Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee all could have moments as well after UCLA's Wayne Knight found some holes in Oregon's defensive line. Knight finished with 103 yards on 22 carries. But this game is also make-or-break for Oregon's postseason hopes, especially with Ohio State and even Northwestern coming up. The Ducks also have a talented roster and, despite their issues, can deliver major blows to opponents when momentum is on their side. Nebraska's issues on the line, in the secondary and even a bit on special teams don't help either. All of this, plus the after-dark setting, provides just enough to tip the scales in the Ducks' favor. Unless Nebraska can truly come out and play like a team that can earn a top-25 spot, this matchup will likely be another so-close-but-so-far loss. away.headline: Is Jamir Conn playing against Oregon? Nebraska football injury update
away.blurb: On Friday night, the Huskers released their second-to-last Big Ten Availability report, and Jamir Conn was on it. Conn, a transfer safety who's been one of the team's best defensive backs since arriving in Lincoln, is officially listed as out. He's joined by Rex Guthrie, who is also out and has missed the majority of the 2026 campaign. Senior defensive tackle Riley Van Poppel, who missed Nebraska's game against Indiana, was also listed as doubtful. In the five games he's played this season, Van Poppel has recorded seven tackles and 2.0 sacks. Jamir Conn and Rex Guthrie ruled out as Nebraska football faces Oregon Other Huskers, including Khamir Prescott, Larry Miles, Jase Reynolds, Jacob Bower, and Gabe Moore, have been ruled out since the start of the year. Junior tight end Carter Nelson is the only previously unavailable player no longer listed on the report, so he could see his first game action since Week 3 against North Dakota. Guthrie has battled injuries this season, with his snaps limited to 42, all in nonconference play. But he seemed like a potentially important option, especially with Conn out , given the 574 snaps he logged last year. Guthrie and Conn being out for the game is especially worrisome, as the safety play this season has left much to be desired. Indiana exploited the safety position last week, scoring two fourth-quarter touchdowns over 40 yards, largely because the safeties seemed to misread the plays and didn't provide over-the-top coverage. A 75-yard score, followed by a 44-yard TD pass, both to wide-open receivers, turned a 17-6 Nebraska lead into a 20-17 Indiana win. If there's any good news on the injury front, Oregon has plenty of its own, with quarterback Dante Moore and starting safety Aaron Flowers ruled out earlier this week. Nebraska's safety issues could also be helped by the absence of Oregon's leading receiver Evan Stewart. The wideout was listed as doubtful on both of the last two availability reports . Dante Moore out and Evan Stewart iffy hands Nebraska an Oregon opening it badly needs The Nebraska football team has yet another massive game on its plate in Saturday night's faceoff against Oregon. Unfortunately, the Huskers are not only banged up, but they'll also go into the game without two of their best safeties and one of their best defensive linemen. Conn played just 17 snaps against the Hoosiers but made several key plays before being injured on the first play of the second half. Junior defensive back Caleb Benning replaced the Kansas City-area native for the rest of the game. Benning could be in line for a larger role against the Ducks, though Nebraska defensive coordinator Aurich has emphasized that Nebraska will prioritize getting its best 11 players on the field rather than simply plugging in the next man up. Junior tight end Carter Nelson is the only previously unavailable player no longer listed on the report, so he could see his first game action since Week 3 against North Dakota. Guthrie has battled injuries this season, with his snaps limited to 42, all in nonconference play. But he seemed like a potentially important option, especially with Conn out , given the 574 snaps he logged last year. Guthrie and Conn being out for the game is especially worrisome, as the safety play this season has left much to be desired. Indiana exploited the safety position last week, scoring two fourth-quarter touchdowns over 40 yards, largely because the safeties seemed to misread the plays and didn't provide over-the-top coverage. A 75-yard score, followed by a 44-yard TD pass, both to wide-open receivers, turned a 17-6 Nebraska lead into a 20-17 Indiana win. If there's any good news on the injury front, Oregon has plenty of its own, with quarterback Dante Moore and starting safety Aaron Flowers ruled out earlier this week. Nebraska's safety issues could also be helped by the absence of Oregon's leading receiver Evan Stewart. The wideout was listed as doubtful on both of the last two availability reports . Dante Moore out and Evan Stewart iffy hands Nebraska an Oregon opening it badly needs The Nebraska football team has yet another massive game on its plate in Saturday night's faceoff against Oregon. Unfortunately, the Huskers are not only banged up, but they'll also go into the game without two of their best safeties and one of their best defensive linemen. Conn played just 17 snaps against the Hoosiers but made several key plays before being injured on the first play of the second half. Junior defensive back Caleb Benning replaced the Kansas City-area native for the rest of the game. Benning could be in line for a larger role against the Ducks, though Nebraska defensive coordinator Aurich has emphasized that Nebraska will prioritize getting its best 11 players on the field rather than simply plugging in the next man up.
